title: Regional priming conductor & probe scorer for warm-standby activation
creator: Marina Gomez
description:
Purpose: build a Regional Priming Conductor (RPC) that scores and orchestrates lightweight readiness probes against warm-standby fleets, producing an activation decision that factors cache warmth, model-variant compatibility, tier affinity, and SLO gating. This ticket implements the probe scoring heuristic, orchestration API, and an initial rollout plan for dry-run shadow activations.

Background: Current warm-standby flow relies on simple liveness pings and manual priming. During cross-region cutovers we see elevated cold-start tail latency when standby caches are cold or incompatible model variants are chosen. We need a deterministic, auditable conductor that: (1) runs probabilistic priming probes with controlled traffic shaping, (2) computes a readiness score combining KV/cache hit estimates, end-to-end p95 latency, model-variant warm compatibility, and recent error rate, and (3) gates activation with quorum and hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping.

Design summary:
- Probe types: control-plane prefill (small synthetic sequences to warm KV cache), inference smoke test (realistic request shape), and gradient probes (edge-case longer-seq samples). Each probe records token throughput, kv-hit-estimate, memory pressure, and model response shape checks.
- Scoring model: weighted aggregation with tunable weights per-customer/tier (weight_kv * kv_hit + weight_p95 * p95_score + weight_variant * compatibility_score + weight_errors * (1 - error_rate)). Scores normalize to 0..100. A configurable threshold plus hysteresis window determines activation.
- Quorum: regional quorum is computed across N standby nodes; activation requires quorum_score >= threshold and at least X% nodes reporting kv_hit_estimate >= warm_kv_threshold.
- Tier routing interaction: RPC exposes an activation_hint that the smart-router uses to prefer same-tier fallback variants (e.g., quantized variant in same tier before moving to cheaper region).
- Rollout mode: start in dry-run shadow mode where conductor emits activation recommendations to the routing service and logs decisions to the console; only after 3 cycles of stable positive recommendations will we enable automated activation for P0 customers under canary.

Implementation plan:
1) New lightweight probe agent binary (rust) deployed as a sidecar to standby pods that can execute prefill and smoke probes without affecting main runtime.
2) RPC service (control-plane) with endpoints: POST /v1/priming/run -> returns probe_result_id; GET /v1/priming/result/{id} -> returns score and diagnostics.
3) Probe scoring library (go) duplicated into routing and console to make decisions reproducible. Export versioned scoring schema so behavior can be audited.
4) Telemetry: new metrics (priming.score, priming.kv_hit_est, priming.p95_ms, priming.error_rate, priming.activation_hint) and a Grafana dashboard.
5) Runbook & rollback: include step-by-step cutover activation and manual disable knobs (circuit-breaker TTL, forced-deactivate endpoint).

Trade-offs and notes:
- Running probes consumes capacity and can affect SLOs if unbounded: we limit probe QPS per node (configurable) and schedule probes during slack windows where possible.
- Scoring complexity vs auditability: we favor a simple linear weighted model (explicit weights) rather than ML so ops can reason about decisions.
- KV warmth is an estimate (we will derive kv_hit_est from recent cache eviction counters and probe observed cache hits; accurate but approximate).

Acceptance criteria:
- Probe agent can run prefill and smoke probes without impacting normal inference (validated with load tests).
- RPC returns reproducible readiness scores for a given probe set and scoring config (unit tests + integration).
- Routing service accepts activation_hint and logs whether it would apply the hint (dry-run).
- Dashboard shows historic priming.score and per-node kv_hit_est.
- Runbook created in Confluence and on-call notified of new playbook.

Operational concerns:
- Cost: probes increase token count; include a cost-metering tag in telemetry so we can track increment.
- Security: probes must not leak customer prompts; default probe corpus is synthetic and audited. If customer-specific priming is enabled, require customer opt-in and KMS audit.

Next steps:
- Spike the probe agent and scoring library (3 days).
- PR for RPC proto and scoring schema (5 days).
- Integration test with staging routing (2 days) and a 1-week dry-run canary on a low-traffic region.

Link to design doc and runbook in attachments.
acceptance_criteria: Probe agent deployed as sidecar performs prefill and smoke probes under load without >1% p99 regression for primary traffic
RPC returns stable readiness_score reproducible across repeated runs with same probe inputs
Routing service logs dry-run decisions for 100% of conductor outputs during canary window
Grafana panel priming.score and per-node kv_hit_est are visible and have alert thresholds configured
Confluence runbook published with step-by-step activation and rollback, assigned to ops on-call
